summary: Disposition round, no code. Closed the two open follow-up proposals that ask the pipeline to refine its own checkers, on the 2026-09-21 operator instruction to clear low-priority work off the recommendation board so the Battle Monster play axis is not queued behind it. The two proposals about runtime behaviour (Jvm::exception's missing floor, whether Jvm::new may panic) are deliberately left open. Declining here is a declaration, not a deletion: the proposals[] elements stay exactly where they are, because that array's 0-based index is the ref.
declineReason: 2026-09-21 운영자 지시 — 배틀몬스터 플레이 집중을 위한 우선순위 정리. Not a judgement that either proposal is wrong: both are checker-refinement work (a product/test split in the exception-name report; a tuple-unpack hole in the output-order lock), and neither is a defect a user can reach. They are being taken off the board, not off the record.
revert: Remove the ref from declinedProposals[] in this file and it is open again on the next scan — the proposal body was never touched. Delete both refs to restore the 2026-09-21 board exactly.

measurements.open_predicate: open = proposals - adopted - declined - injected - dismissed (cockpitd.js collectProposals/scanRepoSimple); injected/dismissed come from ~/tower/data/{injected,dismissed}.json, so a repo-local count alone reads 32, not 4

verification: baseline reproduced the number the ticket quotes: replicating the consumer's predicate over this tree plus tower's two ledgers gives open 4, and names exactly the 4 refs the ticket lists as 2-to-close + 2-to-keep

after: open 2, and the two remaining refs are the two the ticket says to keep (2026-09-20-string-array-hiding-overflows-stack#p0, 2026-09-20-name-the-missing-bootstrap-class#p0) - the keep set was counted, not assumed, so over-pruning would show
no ref drift: the full ref list derived from proposals[] indices is byte-identical before and after (99 refs both ways), because nothing was removed from any proposals[] array
changes: no code, and no edit to either proposal's own worklog file
issues: Declining is recorded in a third file rather than in the file that carries the proposal, following this repo's existing idiom (2026-09-17-ldc-asm-regeneration-declined.json declines a 2026-09-16 proposal). The cost is that a reader opening the proposal's own worklog sees no sign it was closed; the consumer is the only thing that joins them.

The output-order lock's named hole stays open in the docstring of scripts/check-script-output-order.py, and the exception-name report still does not say product vs test. Both remain true after this round; what changed is that neither is on the board asking to be picked up.

The open count depends on tower's injected.json and dismissed.json, which live outside this repo. A future reader re-measuring here alone will get 32 and think this round did nothing - the predicate is recorded above for that reason.
